A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WINO and support a complete comparison of the text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The detailed case studies in v1 are retained in v2 Appendix A.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original WINO accuracy, decoding-speed, memory, ablation, and case-study results on language and vision-language tasks.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark experiments and reports additional verification-threshold and parallel-sampling results.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same parallel drafting and verification procedure, shadow block, position IDs, attention mask, and update rules. Correcting Yshard to Yshad changes notation, not the method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same eight language and six vision-language tasks. V2 identifies MATH more specifically as MATH-500; this does not establish new task or domain coverage. Added analyses use existing benchmarks.

E2.justification: V2 adds naive parallel sampling to the Flickr30K comparison in Figure 1, but drops its MathVista-mini comparison from v1 Table 6. The GSM8K parallel-sampling comparison survives in prose. The principal LLaDA, MMaDA, and Only Draft comparators remain.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes Sudoku from the blanket zero-shot description to 4-shot and narrows the reported drafting-threshold search from {0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7} to {0.5, 0.6, 0.7}. Added evaluations use eight tokens per step on Flickr30K and sweep verification thresholds {0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 0.95}. These reported changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 Figure 4 extends v1 Figure 5's drafting-threshold analysis with verification-threshold sensitivity tests on GSM8K and MMMU-val. The generation-length, full-diffusion, verification-removal, difficulty, memory, and detailed case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional plots continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds verification-threshold results and Flickr30K naive-parallel results of 37.15 CIDEr at 32 steps. It removes the MathVista-mini parallel-sampling entries of 30.02 accuracy at 128 steps and 29.80 at 64 steps. Main benchmark scores and retained ablation results remain unchanged; merged tables and relocated cases are not new results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4) and the stated attention-mask properties retain their mathematical content. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the training-free revokable-decoding contribution and the same headline quality-speed claims, including the GSM8K and Flickr30K improvements.

C2.justification: V2 adds a confidence-based explanation for greater acceleration on easier tasks and discusses robustness to the verification threshold. Appendix B frames the existing dependence on base-model capability as a limitation and proposes training models with draft-and-verify awareness.

D1.justification: V2 provides the more specific MATH-500 identification and revises hyperparameter documentation, but removes the statement that final answers are extracted from reasoning traces. The code and model-checkpoint links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Shi et al. (2024), Simplified and Generalized Masked Diffusion for Discrete Data. The broader positioning relative to diffusion models, caching, and sampling acceleration remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 tightens wording in Sections 4.1 and 5, reorders analysis paragraphs, moves detailed case studies into Appendix A, and adds Appendix B. The overall section sequence and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: Figure 1 gains comparator bars and a legend; Figure 2 rearranges and annotates its panels; threshold plots become combined accuracy/speed displays; and a compact case-study Figure 5 is added. V1 Tables 3–4 are merged, Table 6 is removed, and document typography and layout change throughout.

improvement.justification: The added verification-threshold analysis makes an important parameter choice better assessable, while clearer diagrams, consolidated tables, and more explicit settings improve communication and transparency. These limited gains outweigh the loss of MathVista parallel-sampling results and final-answer extraction detail. The core method and main empirical conclusions remain unchanged.
